item.title: Oyu Stone Circles: Akita's Jomon UNESCO Site — Guide
item.description: The Oyu Stone Circles are two large prehistoric stone rings from the Jomon period, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site within the Jomon Prehistoric Sites of Northern Japan. The Manza and Nonakado circles, some 4,000 years old, feature a striking sundial-like arrangement of standing stones, thought to relate to burial and ritual. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Kazuno, Akita Hours Grounds always open; museum ~9:00–16:00 Admission Free (site); museum small fee Time needed About 1 hour Best time Spring–autumn (green) What to See Two large Jomon stone circles (~4,000 years old).
